en.title: Netflix's October Slate: 3 Must-Watch Movies for Every Fan
en.summary: As October rolls in, Netflix is dropping a diverse slate of films. From Tyler Perry's latest to a genre-bending classic, find your next obsession on the streaming giant.
en.body:
October is here, and with it comes a fresh wave of cinematic treats on Netflix, promising something for every taste. While the big screen might be dominated by blockbuster re-releases and new theatrical arrivals, the streaming world offers a treasure trove of diverse entertainment. This month, Netflix is bringing a mix of anticipated projects and beloved genre flicks that are perfect for cozying up at home.

## Your October Netflix Watchlist

First up, the ever-prolific **Tyler Perry** returns to Netflix with **"Doing Life,"** his third project for the platform this year. While Perry's films don't always land with critics, they consistently capture the attention of a massive audience, making this a likely contender for widespread viewership. Details on the plot remain under wraps, but given Perry's track record, expect a compelling narrative likely exploring themes of life, relationships, and personal journeys.

For those craving something with a bit more bite, **"Pride and Prejudice and Zombies"** makes a welcome appearance. This 2016 cult favorite cleverly mashes up Jane Austen's beloved Regency romance with the undead. The premise is simple yet brilliant: feisty Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr. Darcy must navigate societal expectations and zombie hordes in 19th-century England. It's a witty, action-packed romp that offers a fresh, gory twist on a literary classic, proving that even the most proper ladies can wield a sword with deadly precision.

Beyond these, the streaming service is also adding **"Animals,"** directed by the acclaimed **Ben Affleck**. While specific plot details for this particular film are scarce, Affleck's directorial efforts often showcase a keen eye for character and compelling storytelling. Given his previous successes like **"Argo"** and **"The Town,"** "Animals" is poised to be another strong addition to his filmography, offering a potentially character-driven drama or thriller that fans will want to dissect.

## A Treat for Genre Fans

The fan community is buzzing about the sheer variety on offer. The inclusion of **"Pride and Prejudice and Zombies"** is a particular delight for those who enjoy genre mashups and darkly humorous takes on familiar stories. It’s a film that has cultivated a dedicated following over the years, and its availability on Netflix means a new generation of viewers can discover its unique charm, while existing fans can revisit it on demand. Similarly, the anticipation for any new project from **Tyler Perry** or a directorial effort from **Ben Affleck** underscores the diverse tastes of the Netflix audience, demonstrating a clear demand for both star-driven projects and creatively bold independent films.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for all titles within October are still being finalized, these selections represent just a fraction of what Netflix has planned. Keep an eye out for further announcements regarding other potential additions, including more licensed classics and original series making their debut this fall.

content_raw: After Avengers: Endgame was re-released in global theaters last weekend, cashing in on the hype ahead of December 18's Doomsday , the global box office was once again topped by the MCU. This weekend, a pair of exciting new arrivals will look to take the first October top spot. First, Anne Hathaway , Dakota Johnson , and Josh Hartnett star in Verity , the latest Colleen Hoover adaptation, sure to prove a big hit. Then there's Digger , Tom Cruise 's first non-franchise film in almost a decade, directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu . But if none of these grab your attention, then there's plenty more you could watch from the comfort of your own home. Here's a look at three movies you should watch this weekend on Netflix .
